questions.prompt: Which HTTP methods are idempotent by definition?
questions.explanation: Repeating a GET, PUT or DELETE leaves the resource in the same state. Repeating a POST usually creates another resource, so it needs extra protection such as an idempotency key.
questions.hint: Ask: if the request is sent twice, does anything extra happen?

questions.prompt: A social feed shows 20 posts at a time while new posts keep arriving. Why is cursor pagination better than offset pagination here?

options.text: Cursors compress the response so it downloads faster
With offsets, new posts shift every page, so users see duplicates or miss posts, and deep offsets get slow
Offsets are not allowed in REST APIs

questions.explanation: A cursor marks a position in the data (just after the last item seen), so inserts don't shift the next page and the database can seek straight to it.

questions.prompt: Where does gRPC usually fit best?

options.text: A public API that browsers call directly
High-volume calls between your own backend services

questions.explanation: gRPC's typed schemas, compact binary encoding and streaming suit internal service-to-service traffic. Browsers can't call it directly without a proxy.

questions.prompt: An AI assistant streams its answer to the browser word by word. The browser doesn't send anything while the answer streams. Which option is simplest and fits best?
questions.explanation: Traffic only flows server to client, so SSE is enough: it's plain HTTP, simple to proxy and reconnects automatically. WebSockets would work, but add two-way complexity you don't need.

questions.prompt: Your public API returns a field named userName. You want it called username. What's the safest plan?

options.text: Rename it in the next release; clients should update
Add username alongside userName, mark userName deprecated, watch usage, and remove it later (or only in a new version)
Return username only to clients that send a newer User-Agent

questions.explanation: Renaming breaks every client that reads the old field. Adding the new field, deprecating the old one visibly and removing it only after usage drops (or in /v2) lets clients move at their own pace.
